**Working Document 03 — WKSPSIM 2026**

**Stock:** Anchovy (*Engraulis encrasicolus*) in the southern part of Division 9.a  
(Gulf of Cadiz and southern part of Portugal), ane.27.9aS

**Affiliation:** Instituto Español de Oceanografía (IEO-CSIC), Centro Oceanográfico de Cádiz, Spain

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(knitr)
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)

rds_dir <- here("data", "Rdata")
ref_fig_dir <- here("outputs", "fishery_conditioning", "figures")
ref_tab_dir <- here("outputs", "fishery_conditioning", "tables")
sens_fig_dir <- here("outputs", "fishery_sensitivity", "figures")
sens_tab_dir <- here("outputs", "fishery_sensitivity", "tables")

required_csv <- function(path) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop("Missing WD input: ", path)
  read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)
}

required_file <- function(path) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop("Missing WD input: ", path)
  path
}

seasonal_summary_file <- file.path(ref_tab_dir, "seasonal_catch_allocation_summary.csv")
seasonal_check_file <- file.path(ref_tab_dir, "reference_seasonal_share_check_100OMs.csv")
catch_age_file <- file.path(ref_tab_dir, "historical_catch_at_age_composition_by_quarter_table.csv")

trend_file <- file.path(sens_tab_dir, "seasonal_catch_allocation_trend_results.csv")
break_file <- file.path(sens_tab_dir, "seasonal_catch_allocation_breakpoints.csv")
changepoint_file <- file.path(sens_tab_dir, "seasonal_catch_allocation_changepoints_meanvar.csv")
pca_variance_file <- file.path(sens_tab_dir, "seasonal_catch_allocation_pca_variance.csv")
cluster_file <- file.path(sens_tab_dir, "seasonal_catch_allocation_cluster_summary.csv")
candidate_file <- file.path(sens_tab_dir, "candidate_seasonal_catch_allocation_scenarios.csv")

catch_age_fig_file <- required_file(file.path(ref_fig_dir, "historical_catch_at_age_composition_by_quarter.png"))
trend_fig_file <- required_file(file.path(sens_fig_dir, "seasonal_catch_allocation_trends.png"))
cluster_fig_file <- required_file(file.path(sens_fig_dir, "seasonal_catch_allocation_cluster_means.png"))
candidate_fig_file <- required_file(file.path(sens_fig_dir, "candidate_seasonal_catch_allocation_scenarios.png"))

seasonal_summary <- required_csv(seasonal_summary_file)
seasonal_check <- required_csv(seasonal_check_file)
catch_age_table <- required_csv(catch_age_file)

trend_results <- required_csv(trend_file)
break_results <- required_csv(break_file)
changepoint_results <- required_csv(changepoint_file)
pca_variance <- required_csv(pca_variance_file)
cluster_summary <- required_csv(cluster_file)
candidate_scenarios <- required_csv(candidate_file)

stopifnot(n_distinct(seasonal_check$om) == 100)
stopifnot(n_distinct(seasonal_check$season) == 4)
stopifnot(nrow(seasonal_check) == 400)
stopifnot(all(candidate_scenarios$scenario %in% c("historical", "recent10", "recent3", "cluster_1", "cluster_2", "cluster_3")))
stopifnot(all(abs(candidate_scenarios |> group_by(scenario) |> summarise(total = sum(prop), .groups = "drop") |> pull(total) - 1) < 1e-10))

seasonal_share_max_diff <- max(seasonal_check$abs_diff, na.rm = TRUE)

reference_share <- seasonal_check |>
  group_by(season) |>
  summarise(
    mean_reference_share = mean(reference_share, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_reference_share = sd(reference_share, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

seasonal_summary_table <- seasonal_summary |>
  select(season, mean_prop, sd_prop, p05_prop, p50_prop, p95_prop)

trend_break_table <- trend_results |>
  select(season, slope, p_value_slope, r_squared) |>
  left_join(break_results |> select(season, n_breaks, break_years), by = "season") |>
  left_join(changepoint_results |> select(season, n_changepoints, changepoint_years), by = "season")

pc1_var <- pca_variance |>
  filter(PC == "PC1") |>
  pull(variance_explained)

pc2_var <- pca_variance |>
  filter(PC == "PC2") |>
  pull(variance_explained)

candidate_table <- candidate_scenarios |>
  mutate(season = paste0("Q", season)) |>
  select(scenario, season, prop) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = season, values_from = prop) |>
  arrange(factor(scenario, levels = c("historical", "recent10", "recent3", "cluster_1", "cluster_2", "cluster_3")))

fmt <- function(x, n = 3) formatC(as.numeric(x), format = "f", digits = n)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center",
  out.width = "90%"
)
```

# Fishery conditioning

## General approach

The fishery component of the Operating Model (OM) was constructed from the
conditioned ane.27.9aS trajectories described in WD01. The fishery is
represented in FLBEIA by one fleet (`SEINE`), one métier (`ALL`), and one
exploited stock (`ANE`) [@Garcia2017FLBEIA].

Historical fishery variables were transferred from the SS3 bootstrap
realizations, maintaining the correspondence between the population and
fishery of each OM. The historical period covers 1989--2024 and the
projection covers 2025--2054. The 100 historical conditions were expanded
to 1,000 trajectories, with 10 replicates per OM.

For the projection, catchability, fleet variables, and seasonal catch
allocation were parameterized from recent historical periods. Effort,
fishing mortality, and realized catches during the projection are
subsequently generated within the FLBEIA simulations.

The reference seasonal allocation was defined from the quarterly catch
proportions observed during 2015--2024. Historical variation in these
proportions was examined to define alternative patterns subsequently used
in the robustness analysis.

# Methods {#methods}

## Historical fishery structure

The historical fishery remains associated with each biological OM
condition. Thus, differences among OMs are not limited to population state
and dynamics; each OM also retains the catch history corresponding to its
SS3 bootstrap refit.

The 100 historical conditions were expanded to 1,000 trajectories,
maintaining the correspondence between each projection trajectory and its
source OM. Numbers and weights at age for landings and discards were
transferred to the FLBEIA fishery component through an `FLCatchExt`,
integrated into métier `ALL` and fleet `SEINE`.

In SS3, the weight at age used for the stock and catch is the same. This assumption was retained during conversion to FLBEIA by checking, for each OM, the correspondence between `landings.wt` and the weight at age of the biological component (`wt`). A maximum absolute-difference tolerance of \(10^{-10}\) was used.

## Fleet variables and projection assumptions

The projected fishery retains the historically conditioned fleet
structure, whereas effort and catches are determined dynamically during the
simulation. The fleet object includes the `effort.share`, `vcost`, `effort`,
`capacity`, `crewshare`, and `fcost` components.

For 2025--2054, `landings.wt`, `discards.wt`, `vcost`, `fcost`, and
`crewshare` were fixed from the iteration-specific 2022--2024 mean.
Thus, the conditions used during the projection retain differences among
OMs derived from historical conditioning.

In the configuration used, `vcost` and `effort` were set to 1,
`capacity` to 5,000, and `crewshare` and `fcost` to 0. `effort.share` was
retained from the input file. `alpha`, `beta`, `effort.share`, and `capacity`
were initially extended from historical values. During the projection,
`beta` and `effort` were initialized at 1, whereas `landings.n` and
`discards.n` were initialized at 0.

These values define the initial fishery conditions. Effort, fishing
mortality, and realized catches during 2025--2054 are subsequently
determined within the FLBEIA simulations.


## Effort and catch models

During the projection, the fishery responds to the target catch established
by the management procedure through adjustment of fishing effort. The
relationship between effort and stock exploitation is represented through
catchability (`catch.q`), whereas realized catch is calculated from stock
abundance and natural and fishing mortality using the Baranov catch equation.

In FLBEIA, this dynamic is implemented using `SMFB` as the effort model
and `Baranov` as the catch model [@Garcia2017FLBEIA]. The effort constraint
is linked to stock `ANE` and specified in terms of catch.

Catchability (`catch.q`) was calculated for each OM using the 2020--2024
period and kept constant during 2025--2054. Therefore, differences among OMs
in this component are retained during the projection. Non-finite values
obtained when calculating `catch.q` were replaced by zero.

Fleet capacity was kept constant through `fixedCapital`, with
`capacity = 5000`. `catch.threshold` was set to 0.9 and `alpha` to 1.

Catch was assigned to landings (`landings.sel = 1`) and discards were not
modeled (`discards.sel = 0`). The discard mechanism associated with catches
above quota was also disabled (`discard.TAC.OS = FALSE`).

## Reference seasonal catch allocation

The OM is structured into four quarters and, therefore, annual catch must
be distributed among the four seasons. This allocation determines when
exploitation occurs within the year and its temporal relationship with
population dynamics, including spawning in Q2 and recruitment entry in Q3.

Seasonal allocation is expressed as the proportion of annual catch
occurring in each quarter. For OM \(i\), year \(y\), and quarter
\(s\), this proportion is calculated as

\[
p_{iys} =
\frac{C_{iys}}
{\sum_{s=1}^{4} C_{iys}},
\]

where \(C_{iys}\) is the biomass caught in quarter \(s\). The four
proportions sum to one for each OM-year combination.

For the reference configuration, the seasonal allocation of each OM was
defined as the mean of the quarterly proportions observed during
2015--2024:

\[
\bar{p}_{is}^{\,2015:2024}
=
\frac{1}{10}
\sum_{y=2015}^{2024} p_{iys}.
\]

The resulting four proportions were retained during 2025--2054 for the
corresponding OM. Thus, this parameterization determines the distribution
of catch among quarters, but not the magnitude of annual catch, which is
determined during the simulation.

Each of the 100 OMs retains its own 2015--2024 seasonal allocation.
The ten replicates derived from the same OM share these proportions. For
historical diagnostics, one representative trajectory per OM was used,
avoiding treatment of replicates as independent historical observations.

Implementation was checked by reconstructing the mean 2015--2024
proportions from historical catches and comparing them with the values
stored in `fleets.ctrl`. A maximum absolute-difference tolerance of
\(10^{-10}\) was used.

## Historical catch by age and quarter

The age composition of catch describes which ages contribute to
exploitation in each quarter and allows its variation during the historical
period to be characterized.

For each OM, year, and quarter, catch at age was calculated as the sum of
landed and discarded numbers. The numbers caught at each age were then
expressed as a proportion of the total catch in the quarter.

These proportions were used only to describe the historical age
composition of the conditioned fishery. They were not used to fix catch
composition during 2025--2054. During the projection, catch at age is
determined dynamically from population structure and simulated exploitation
in FLBEIA.

## Diagnostics of temporal variation in seasonal allocation

The distribution of catches among quarters may vary over time, changing
when exploitation occurs within the year. Because the reference configuration
uses the mean 2015--2024 allocation, the historical series was examined to
characterize its temporal variation and determine whether patterns different
from that used in REF exist.

Diagnostics were based on the annual mean quarterly proportions of the
100 historical OMs. For each quarter, change in the catch proportion over
time was evaluated using a linear regression against year. Changes in the
series were also examined using `strucchange::breakpoints()` and
`changepoint::cpt.meanvar()`, the latter using PELT with an MBIC penalty.

The distribution of catch among the four quarters was also analyzed
jointly. Principal component analysis (PCA) was applied to centered and
scaled annual quarterly proportions to summarize the main changes in
seasonal allocation. Hierarchical clustering was then applied to the scaled
proportions, using Euclidean distance and Ward's method (`ward.D2`), to
group years with similar seasonal distributions.

Three groups (\(k=3\)) were used to summarize contrasting historical
patterns and define alternative seasonal-allocation configurations. These
groups are used as a tool to characterize historical variability and are
not interpreted as three discrete fishery regimes.

These diagnostics do not modify the reference configuration. The identified
historical patterns are subsequently used to define alternative
seasonal-allocation configurations in the sensitivity/robustness analysis.

## Seasonal patterns for the robustness analysis

Alternative patterns for distributing annual catch among the four quarters
were defined from historical variability. These patterns represent different
timings of exploitation within the year without, by themselves, modifying
the magnitude of annual catch.

The patterns were obtained from the mean of the full historical period,
the 2015--2024 mean, the 2022--2024 mean, and the means of the three groups
identified by clustering. Each vector was normalized so that the four
quarterly proportions summed to one.

The reference configuration uses the 2015--2024 mean. For the sensitivity
analysis, the patterns corresponding to clusters 1 and 2, denoted S-C1 and
S-C2, were also selected. These patterns retain the historical structure
observed in each group and allow the effect of modifying the within-year
temporal distribution of exploitation to be evaluated subsequently.

WD03 documents the construction and historical origin of these patterns.
Their implementation and effects on MSE performance are evaluated in WD08.


# Results {#results}


## Reference seasonal allocation

The 2015--2024 seasonal means reconstructed from historical catches
matched the values stored in the reference fleet control object. The maximum
absolute difference was
`r format(seasonal_share_max_diff, scientific = TRUE)`, compared with the
implementation criterion of \(10^{-10}\).

Across the 100 historical OMs, the mean reference allocation was
`r paste0("Q", reference_share$season, " = ", sprintf("%.3f", reference_share$mean_reference_share), collapse = "; ")` (Table \@ref(tab:table-reference-seasonal-share) ).



```{r table-reference-seasonal-share}
kable(
  reference_share,
  digits = 3,
  col.names = c("Quarter", "Mean reference share", "SD among OMs"),
  caption = "Seasonal catch allocation used in the reference projection. Values assigned to each OM correspond to its own 2015--2024 mean; the table summarizes these OM-specific values for the 100 historical OMs."
)
```

## Historical variation in seasonal allocation

The distribution of exploitation among quarters varied during 1989--2024.
Table \@ref(tab:table-seasonal-summary) summarizes the catch proportions
observed across OMs and years and describes the magnitude of this variation
in each quarter.

```{r table-seasonal-summary}
kable(
  seasonal_summary_table,
  digits = 3,
  col.names = c("Quarter", "Mean", "SD", "5%", "Median", "95%"),
  caption = "Historical seasonal catch-allocation proportions for the 100 conditioned OMs and years 1989--2024."
)
```

Temporal diagnostics describe how the contribution of each quarter to
annual catch changed during the historical period. Table
\@ref(tab:table-seasonal-temporal) presents the linear trends and changes
identified in the quarterly series.

These results characterize historical variation in the temporal
distribution of exploitation. The reference configuration retains the
OM-specific 2015--2024 mean.

```{r table-seasonal-temporal}
trend_break_display <- trend_break_table |>
  mutate(
    slope = round(slope, 5),
    p_value_slope = signif(p_value_slope, 3),
    r_squared = round(r_squared, 3)
  ) |>
  rename(
    Quarter = season,
    Slope = slope,
    `p-value` = p_value_slope,
    `R2` = r_squared,
    Breaks = n_breaks,
    `Break years` = break_years,
    Changes = n_changepoints,
    `Change years` = changepoint_years
  )

kable(
  trend_break_display,
  format = "latex",
  booktabs = TRUE,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Temporal diagnostics of historical seasonal catch allocation. The diagnostics characterize the historical series and are not used to redefine the reference OM."
)
```

```{r fig-seasonal-trends, out.width="85%", fig.align="center", fig.cap="Annual seasonal catch-allocation proportions and quarter-specific linear trends during 1989--2024. The diagnostic is based on annual mean proportions across the 100 conditioned OMs."}
knitr::include_graphics(trend_fig_file)
```

## Multivariate seasonal patterns

The first two principal components explained, respectively,
`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * pc1_var)`% and
`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * pc2_var)`% of the variation in the scaled quarterly
proportions, and
`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * (pc1_var + pc2_var))`% jointly.

Hierarchical clustering with \(k=3\) grouped years with similar quarterly
distributions and produced three mean seasonal-allocation patterns. These
groups summarize different historical configurations of the temporal
distribution of exploitation and were used to construct patterns for the
robustness analysis. They are not interpreted as three chronological fishery
regimes.

```{r table-cluster-means}
cluster_table <- cluster_summary |>
  select(cluster, season, mean_prop) |>
  mutate(season = paste0("Q", season)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = season, values_from = mean_prop)

kable(
  cluster_table,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Mean quarterly catch-allocation proportions for the three diagnostic historical clusters."
)
```

```{r fig-cluster-means, fig.cap="Mean quarterly catch-allocation proportions for the three historical groups. The groups are used to construct alternative seasonal-allocation patterns and do not modify the reference OM."}
knitr::include_graphics(cluster_fig_file)
```

## Seasonal patterns for the robustness analysis

Six seasonal-allocation patterns were obtained from the historical
diagnostics: the 1989--2024 mean, the 2015--2024 mean, the 2022--2024 mean,
and the means of the three groups identified by clustering.

Each pattern represents a different distribution of annual catch among
Q1--Q4. The reference configuration retains OM-specific 2015--2024 means.
Therefore, the aggregated `recent10` pattern is used only as a summary of
this period and does not replace the OM-specific proportions used in REF.

The patterns corresponding to clusters 1 and 2 are subsequently used as
S-C1 and S-C2 in the robustness analysis documented in WD08.

```{r table-candidate-seasonal-patterns}
kable(
  candidate_table,
  digits = 3,
  col.names = c("Scenario", "Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4"),
  caption = "Candidate seasonal catch-allocation patterns generated from the historical diagnostics. The reference OM retains OM-specific 2015--2024 means rather than replacing them with the single aggregated recent10 vector shown here."
)
```

```{r fig-candidate-seasonal-patterns, out.width="85%", fig.align="center", fig.cap="Candidate seasonal catch-allocation patterns generated from the historical diagnostics. These patterns define possible sensitivity scenarios; their effects on MSE performance are evaluated subsequently."}
knitr::include_graphics(candidate_fig_file)
```



## Historical catch by age and quarter

Catch age composition differed among quarters during the historical period.
Table \@ref(tab:table-catch-age) summarizes the mean contribution of each
age to quarterly catch in the conditioned OMs.

These proportions describe the age structure of historical exploitation.
They are not used as a fixed composition during the projection, in which
catch at age is determined from the available population and simulated
exploitation in FLBEIA.

```{r table-catch-age}
catch_age_display <- catch_age_table
names(catch_age_display) <- sub("Age_3$", "Age_3plus", names(catch_age_display))

kable(
  catch_age_display,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Mean historical catch composition by age and quarter across conditioned OMs and historical years. Age 3 represents the 3+ group."
)
```

```{r fig-catch-age, out.width="80%", fig.align="center", fig.cap="Mean historical catch composition by age and quarter across conditioned OMs. Catch at age is a historical diagnostic; future realized catch at age is generated dynamically during FLBEIA simulations."}
knitr::include_graphics(catch_age_fig_file)
```


# Reproducibility

The reference fishery is constructed using `10_built_fleet_Reference.R` after generating the biological OM and recruitment-conditioning objects. The script reads the conditioned biological and stock objects, the 1,000-iteration map, and the CSV files containing SEINE fleet variables. It generates:

- `data/Rdata/ane_stock_conditioned_1000iter.rds`;
- `data/Rdata/fleets_conditioned_1000iter.rds`;
- `data/Rdata/fleets_ctrl_reference_1000iter.rds`.

Subsequently, `11_seasonal_catch_allocation_diagnostics.R` reads the conditioned stock, fleet, fleet controls, and iteration map. Reference documentation outputs are stored in `outputs/fishery_conditioning/`, whereas temporal diagnostics, PCA, clustering, and candidate scenarios are stored separately in `outputs/fishery_sensitivity/`.

The main reference settings are summarized in Table \@ref(tab:table-reference-settings).

```{r table-reference-settings}
reference_settings <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Component, ~Reference_setting,
  "Historical period", "1989-2024",
  "Projection period", "2025-2054",
  "Fleet / metier / stock", "SEINE / ALL / ANE",
  "Historical OM conditions", "100",
  "Projection trajectories", "1000 (10 per historical OM)",
  "Effort model", "SMFB",
  "Catch model", "Baranov",
  "Effort restriction", "catch (ANE)",
  "Capital model", "fixedCapital",
  "Catch threshold", "0.9",
  "Catchability averaging period", "2020-2024",
  "Projection weight/fleet averaging period", "2022-2024",
  "Reference seasonal-share averaging period", "2015-2024, OM-specific",
  "landings.sel", "1",
"discards.sel", "0",
"discard.TAC.OS", "FALSE",
  "Future landings.n / discards.n", "initialised at 0",
  "Future beta / effort", "initialised at 1",
  "Future realised catch-at-age", "generated dynamically during simulation"
)

kable(
  reference_settings,
  caption = "Main settings used to construct the reference OM fishery component."
)
```

# Conclusions

- The fishery was incorporated into the OM while maintaining the correspondence
  between each biological condition and the fishery history derived from the
  same SS3 bootstrap refit. During the projection, effort, fishing mortality,
  and catches are generated dynamically in FLBEIA.

- The reference configuration allocates most annual catch to Q2 and Q3, which
  together account for approximately 75% of the catch. This recent pattern
  shows little variation among the 100 OMs and is retained during 2025--2054
  on an OM-specific basis.

- Seasonal allocation was not constant during 1989--2024. The main changes
  were observed in Q1 and Q3, with a decrease in the contribution of Q1 and
  an increase in Q3. Multivariate analyses identified different historical
  patterns in the distribution of catch among quarters.

- Catch age composition also shows a seasonal structure. Q1 and Q2 catches
  are dominated by age-1 individuals, whereas the contribution of age 0
  increases in Q3 and constitutes the largest proportion of catch in Q4.
  This historical composition is not imposed during the projection.

- Historical variability in seasonal allocation was used to define
  alternative exploitation patterns. The patterns corresponding to clusters
  1 and 2 were selected as S-C1 and S-C2 to subsequently evaluate MSE
  sensitivity to changes in the within-year temporal distribution of
  exploitation.
